I still want this for the V2 form flow. During UI review and grilling, a structured question often needs a screenshot as the custom response. Without attachment support, the practical escape hatch is to cancel the form and send a free-form prompt, which loses the structured flow and any in-progress answers.

If the architecture permits it, I would prefer attachments to remain separate from scalar `Form.Answer` values and be associated with the relevant field, rather than encoding an image or temporary path as the answer string. This can be follow-up work and does not need to block the current question-form UX changes.

Closing after an end-to-end A/B benchmark found no measurable production startup improvement. The lazy boundary instead added a repeatable 11-15 ms penalty to the first HTML conversion, so the additional complexity is not justified.

Same root cause as #37435, and its PR (#37477) covers `session list` only — so the export half here is complementary: the same one-line pattern on a different command. The import half is the part that sweep can't take mechanically: import writes a session row whose project_id row only exists because the instance boot created it (foreign_keys is ON), so import needs the project row ensured before it can drop the instance. That contract question is what this issue is really asking.

> Seconding the [#40095](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/40095) lead — opencode-go hangs when outbound connectivity stalls, and WSL's default NAT setup has flaky IPv6/DNS that produces exactly this "stream starts, never returns" pattern. Test with a plain `curl -v --max-time 10` to the gateway endpoint from inside WSL, and try disabling IPv6 on the interface (`sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1`) or pinning a DNS server. If the curl stalls too, it's the WSL network layer, not the provider.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #40998: Also crashes with `UnknownError` / "Unexpected server error" when resolving a custom agent — same symptom of agent lookup failing silently, though that report is via the HTTP API's `agent` body field rather than the CLI `--agent` key. The underlying agent resolution logic may be shared.

Thanks for the check — after comparing against #40998, I believe these are **not duplicates**. The triggers are in different code paths with different conditions:

**#40998 (HTTP API path):**
- Trigger: `POST /session/{id}/message` with an `agent` field in the body → crash in `SessionPrompt.createUserMessage`
- Its reporter explicitly notes the CLI `run`/`--agent` flag "works correctly" in their case — i.e. their bug is specific to the API message-body path
- No mention of the agent's `name` field; it crashes for any `agent` in the body

**#42507 (CLI run path, this one):**
- Trigger: `opencode run --agent <key>` — the exact path #40998 says works
- Fails **only** when the custom agent's config has a `name` field (display name ≠ config key). Custom agents without `name` resolve fine via `--agent` (verified: a key-only custom agent ran normally; adding `name` made the same lookup fail)
- Session is created with `agent=undefined` → "Unexpected server error"; passing the display name instead gives "agent not found, falling back to default"
- Reproduces with `--pure`, so it's core, not plugin-related

So the two reports cover distinct failure modes of agent-name resolution: the API message-body lookup (#40998) and the CLI `--agent` lookup when the display name differs from the key (#42507). Both are worth keeping open; I'd suggest cross-linking them so maintainers see the pattern (agent resolution by name is fragile in both paths). Happy to add a note to #40998 pointing here if that helps.

Another affected client: **Grok Build** (xai-org/grok-build). With a BYOK custom model pointing at `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` (`api_backend = "responses"`), the `ping` keepalive event kills the whole stream — the client's strict event enum rejects it and the turn fails outright:

```
Internal error: serialization error: unknown variant `ping`, expected one of `response.created`, `response.in_progress`, ... `error`
```

Confirmed 2026-08-14 with `deepseek-v4-flash`. Non-streaming `POST /responses` works (returns a complete object), which matches your report — only streaming breaks. Same missing `response.created` / `response.output_item.added` / `response.content_part.added` symptoms.

A graceful fix on the gateway side (drop `ping` or send it as a valid Responses event, and emit the full lifecycle) would fix every strict Responses-API client at once.

Reproduces outside Codex too, and on **flash**, not just v4-pro: **Grok Build**'s `web_search` tool makes a non-streaming `POST /v1/responses` call with `tools: [{type: "web_search"}]` against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` (BYOK, `deepseek-v4-flash`). The response fails to deserialize in the client with:

```
Failed to parse response: missing field `query`
```

So the search tool errors on every call (the agent then falls back to other search methods). For comparison, the same request against the DeepSeek official API (`https://api.deepseek.com/responses`, `deepseek-v4-flash`) succeeds end-to-end — which points to the zen/go conversion layer being the inconsistent part, not the upstream provider.

This looks like the same family of bug as #40171 / PR #40210: the `/v1/responses` path on zen/go doesn't round-trip the OpenAI Responses shapes faithfully (missing/renamed fields, incomplete SSE lifecycle).

Recurred ~25 min after filing, same build (next-17403), same error signature on the **no-data** path:

```
Error: Orphan text error: "Usage: no data yet — chat to track tokens" must have a <text> as a parent: box-3763 above text-node-9238
    at w$ (../../node_modules/.bun/@opentui+solid@0.5.2+b9027845aeff97b0/node_modules/@opentui/solid/index.bun.js:559:17)
    ...
    at <anonymous> (../../tui/src/plugin/context.tsx:74:5)
```

So the crash hits both code paths (empty state and populated state) — any render of the slot payload crashes the TUI, not just data-rich renders.

**Local workaround for the `OPENTUI_FORCE_WCWIDTH already registered` import blocker** — confirmed working on next-17403: clear the host's env-registry singleton before importing `@opentui/solid`:

```js
const sym = Symbol.for("@opentui/core/singleton");
if (globalThis[sym] && globalThis[sym]["env-registry"]) {
  delete globalThis[sym]["env-registry"];
}
solid = await import("@opentui/solid");
```

With that, slot `render()` can return proper element trees built via `createElement("box")` / `createElement("text")` + `setProp`/`insert` (solid universal API re-exported by `@opentui/solid`), and the orphan-text crash disappears. If the import still fails, returning `null` from `render()` is tolerated by the host (renders nothing, no crash).

Host-side fixes still warranted regardless:

1. A plain string returned from a slot `render()` should be wrapped in a `<text>` node (or rejected with a per-slot error) instead of crashing the whole TUI.
2. The `@opentui/core` singleton collision shouldn't be reachable from plugin module code — plugins loading a second copy of the bundled deps is a normal resolution outcome.

When configuring a vision-capable model through an OpenAI-compatible provider (e.g., llama.cpp, LM Studio, Jan), setting `"vision": true` in the model config has **no effect** — images pasted in interactive sessions fail with:

Cannot read 'clipboard' (this model does not support image input).

The model clearly supports vision (verified via direct curl to the same endpoint). The issue is that opencode does not recognize `vision: true` as the capability flag for OpenAI-compatible providers.

### Solution

The correct config requires **both** `attachment: true` and explicit `modalities`:

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "llamacpp": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "llama.cpp",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://localhost:8080/v1",
        "apiKey": "local"
      },
      "models": {
        "Qwen3.6-35B-A3B": {
          "name": "Qwen3.6-35B-A3B",
          "attachment": true,
          "modalities": {
            "input": ["text", "image"],
            "output": ["text"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Key differences:
- ❌ "vision": true — has no effect, model vision not detected
- ✅ "attachment": true — this is the correct flag
- ✅ "modalities": { "input": ["text", "image"], "output": ["text"] } — required for full detection
Important: Restart Required
Opencode caches model capabilities on startup. After updating opencode.json, you must restart the process:
pkill opencode && sleep 2 && opencode
Without a restart, the cached (non-vision) capabilities persist.
Proposed Fixes for OpenCode
1. Hot-reload config: Detect changes to opencode.json and reload model capabilities without requiring a full restart.
2. Auto-detect vision: Check for mmproj files (LM Studio) or multimodal model names on startup and automatically enable the vision pipeline.
3. Better error message: Instead of "this model does not support image input", show: "this model has vision capabilities but vision is not enabled. Try adding attachment: true and modalities to your provider config, then restart opencode."
4. Document the correct config: The vision: true flag is misleading for OpenAI-compatible providers. Either support it as an alias for attachment: true, or deprecate it in favor of the working approach.
Environment
- OpenCode version: 1.18.x
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (local, via llama.cpp)
- Provider: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible
- OS: Linux
